title: ever / never / already / yet / just
grammarTitle: Present Perfect: ever / never / already / yet / just
grammarNote:
Пять ключевых наречий Present Perfect — каждое со своим значением и позицией:

① ALREADY — уже (раньше ожидаемого):
   Позиция: между have и participle
   "I have already done my homework." (уже сделал — раньше чем ожидалось)
   "She has already left." (уже ушла)

② JUST — только что (совсем недавно):
   Позиция: между have и participle
   "I have just finished lunch." (только что закончил)
   "He has just arrived." (только что приехал)

③ YET — уже/ещё (в вопросах и отрицаниях):
   Позиция: В КОНЦЕ предложения!
   В вопросе: "Have you finished yet?" (уже закончил?)
   В отрицании: "I haven't finished yet." (ещё не закончил)

④ EVER — когда-нибудь (в вопросах об опыте):
   Позиция: между have и participle
   "Have you ever been to London?" (когда-нибудь бывал?)
   "Has she ever tried beshbarmak?" (когда-нибудь пробовала?)

⑤ NEVER — никогда (отрицание опыта):
   Позиция: между have и participle
   "I have never eaten sushi." (никогда не ел)
   "He has never been abroad." (никогда не был за рубежом)

💡 Схема позиций:
Have + ALREADY/JUST/EVER/NEVER + participle
Have + participle + YET Mastering their position and meaning is essential for natural English.

grammarTable.subject: ever
grammarTable.verb: questions only — between have and past participle
grammarTable.short: at any time in your life
grammarTable.example: Have you EVER tried kokpar? Has she EVER been to Almaty?

grammarTable.subject: never
grammarTable.verb: positive form — between have and past participle
grammarTable.example: I have NEVER seen snow. She has NEVER eaten horsemeat.

grammarTable.subject: already
grammarTable.verb: positive form — between have and past participle
grammarTable.example: I have ALREADY finished. She has ALREADY left.

grammarTable.subject: yet
grammarTable.verb: negatives and questions — end of sentence
grammarTable.example: I haven't booked YET. Have you packed YET?

grammarTable.subject: just
grammarTable.verb: positive — between have and past participle
grammarTable.example: She has JUST arrived. He has JUST called.

grammarTable.subject: still
grammarTable.verb: negative — between subject and have (not yet done)
grammarTable.example: She still hasn't replied. He still hasn't eaten.

grammarTable.subject: so far
grammarTable.short: up to this point in time
grammarTable.example: I have crossed off five items SO FAR.

grammarTable.subject: recently
grammarTable.example: She has recently started hiking. RECENTLY, she has started hiking.

rows.form: "ever" = at any time in your life — ONLY in questions
rows.example: Have you ever been to Almaty? / Has she ever tried horseback riding?

rows.form: "never" = not at any time — in positive sentences (means negative)
rows.example: I have never tried skydiving. (= I haven't ever tried skydiving.)

rows.form: Position: between "have/has" and the past participle
rows.example: I have NEVER seen... / Have you EVER tried...? ✓ / Never have I seen... (literary)

rows.form: Don't use "never" in negative sentences
rows.example: I have never not gone. ✗ / I've never gone. ✓ / I haven't ever gone. ✓

rows.form: Superlative + ever
rows.example: It's the best film I've ever seen. / The most terrifying thing I've ever experienced.

rows.form: "Have you ever?" — short answers
rows.example: Yes, I have! / No, I never have. / No, I haven't.

rows.form: "already" = done sooner than expected (positive sentences + questions)
rows.example: She's ALREADY finished! (surprised it's so early)

rows.form: "yet" = expected but not done (negatives and questions)
rows.example: I haven't packed YET. / Have you booked YET? (expected action)

rows.form: Position of "already": between have/has and participle
rows.example: I have ALREADY eaten. / She has ALREADY left.

rows.form: Position of "yet": at the END of the sentence
rows.example: I haven't eaten YET. / Have you eaten YET?

rows.form: "yet" in questions = expecting the action to be done
rows.example: Has she heard back yet? (= I expect she will hear back)

rows.form: "already" in questions = surprised it happened so soon
rows.example: Have you already finished?! (= That's fast! I didn't expect it.)

rows.form: "just" = a very short time ago (minutes / hours)
rows.example: She's JUST arrived. / He's JUST called.

rows.form: "recently" = not long ago (days / weeks, no exact time)
rows.example: I've recently started yoga. / She's recently moved to Uralsk.

rows.form: Position of "just": between have/has and past participle
rows.example: She has JUST finished. ✓ / She has finished JUST. ✗

rows.form: Position of "recently": flexible (start or end)
rows.example: RECENTLY, she has started hiking. / She has started hiking RECENTLY.

rows.form: Both signal "no specific time" → Present Perfect (not Past Simple)
rows.example: She has just arrived. ✓ / She just arrived. ✓ (informal only)

rows.form: "just" emphasises immediacy
rows.example: The train has JUST left — you'll catch the next one. (only seconds ago)

rows.form: have + EVER + past participle?
rows.example: Have you EVER tried...? Has she EVER seen...?

rows.form: have + NEVER + past participle
rows.example: I have NEVER eaten... She has NEVER been...

rows.form: have + ALREADY + past participle
rows.example: I have ALREADY finished. She has ALREADY left.

rows.form: have + JUST + past participle
rows.example: He has JUST called. They have JUST arrived.

rows.form: haven't/hasn't + past participle + YET
rows.example: I haven't packed YET. She hasn't replied YET.

rows.form: Have/Has + subject + past participle + YET?
rows.example: Have you packed YET? Has she replied YET?

grammarTip:
Позиции пяти ключевых наречий Present Perfect:

ALREADY, JUST, EVER, NEVER → между have/has и participle:
"I have ALREADY done it." · "She has JUST left."
"Have you EVER seen it?" · "I have NEVER been abroad."

❗ Только YET → В КОНЕЦ предложения:
"Have you done it YET?" · "I haven't finished YET."

💡 Мнемоника: YET = "ещё нет?" или "уже ли?" → задаёт вопрос в конце

exercises.hint: "Ever" goes between "have" and the past participle in questions about life experience.

exercises.text: I ___ been to Scotland. It's on my bucket list!
exercises.hint: "Never" = not at any time. Used in positive-form sentences to express "not ever".

exercises.text: She has ___ finished her essay. She's very fast!
exercises.hint: "Already" = sooner than expected. Position: between has and past participle.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct word for the negative.
exercises.text: I haven't booked my hiking boots ___.
exercises.hint: "Yet" = expected but not done. Goes at the END of negative sentences.

exercises.text: She has ___ arrived — she walked through the door two minutes ago!
exercises.hint: "Just" = a very short time ago. Goes between has and past participle.

exercises.instruction: Find the sentence with the correct word order.
opts: I have yet packed my bag.
I haven't packed my bag yet.
I have packed yet my bag.
I haven't yet packed my bag yet.
exercises.correct: I haven't packed my bag yet.
exercises.hint: "Yet" goes at the END of negative sentences. Between the auxiliary and participle is wrong for "yet".

exercises.text: Have you eaten ___? — Yes, I've ___ eaten. I finished an hour ago.
exercises.hint: Question: "...yet?" (end). Answer: "I've already eaten" (between have and participle).
"Never" goes between "have" and the past participle. Do NOT combine with "haven't" (double negative).

exercises.text: This is the most beautiful place I've ___ seen!
exercises.hint: "The most/best... I've ever seen/done" — superlative + ever is a fixed collocation.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct word for this question.
exercises.text: Has Kamila heard back from the university ___?
exercises.hint: "Yet" at the end of a question = is the expected action done?

exercises.text: He has ___ published his first novel — I saw it in the bookshop yesterday!
exercises.hint: "Recently" = not long ago (no exact time). Goes with Present Perfect for recent events.
"Just" goes between "has" and the past participle: has + just + past participle.

questions.hint: "Ever" goes in questions: Have you EVER tried...?

questions.text: I ___ seen the Northern Lights. It's my biggest dream!
questions.hint: "Never" = at no time. Position: have + NEVER + past participle.

questions.text: She has ___ finished packing — she's very organised!
questions.hint: "Already" = sooner than expected. Position: has + ALREADY + past participle.
"Yet" = expected but not done. Goes at the END of negative sentences.

questions.text: He has ___ called — I can hear his voice outside the door!
questions.hint: "Just" = a very short time ago (seconds/minutes). Position: has + JUST + past participle.

questions.text: "I haven't never done it" is correct English.
questions.hint: Double negative is incorrect. Use either: "I haven't done it" OR "I have never done it."
"Yet" at the end of a question = asking if the expected action has been done.

questions.text: It's the best concert I've ___ been to!
questions.hint: "The best/most... I've ever..." — superlative + ever is a fixed pattern.
"Just" goes between auxiliary (has) and past participle: has + JUST + called.

questions.text: Which word expresses "not at any time in your life"?
questions.hint: "Never" = not at any time. Used in positive-form present perfect sentences.

questions.text: "Already" can go at the end of a sentence (I've finished already).
questions.hint: "Already" can also go at the end, though it more commonly goes before the participle. Both are correct.

questions.text: She has ___ arrived home — she left the office just three minutes ago.
questions.hint: "Just" = a very short time ago (she left only 3 minutes ago).

questions.text: Has the result come out ___? — No, not ___!
questions.hint: "Yet" at end of question and at end of negative: "No, not yet!"

opts: Present Perfect for recent events with no exact time
questions.correct: Present Perfect for recent events with no exact time
questions.hint: "Recently" signals a vague recent time → Present Perfect. No exact time mentioned.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses "already" in a question?
questions.hint: "Already" in a question = surprised the action happened so soon: "Have you already...?"

opts: She has never not been to Paris.
She has never been to Paris.
She never has been to Paris.
She has been to Paris never.
questions.correct: She has never been to Paris.
questions.hint: Position: has + NEVER + past participle. No double negatives.
